sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ pṛthu vṛkṣā mahāyaśāḥ uvāca rāmaḥ saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam
english: When the night had brightened into dawn, the great-famed Rāma, standing by the broad trees, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, that one bearing auspicious marks.

sanskrit: bhāskarodayakālo 'yaṃ gatā bhagavatī niśā asau sukṛṣṇo vihagaḥ kokilas tāta kūjati
english: "The hour of the sun's rising is come; the blessed night has departed. There, dear one, that dark-plumaged bird, the kokila, calls out."

sanskrit: barhiṇānāṃ ca nirghoṣaḥ śrūyate nadatāṃ vane tarāma jāhnavīṃ saumya śīghragāṃ sāgaraṃgamām
english: "The cry of peacocks is heard calling in the forest. Let us cross the Jāhnavī, dear friend — swift-flowing, bound for the ocean."

sanskrit: vijñāya rāmasya vacaḥ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ guham āmantrya sūtaṃ ca so 'tiṣṭhad bhrātur agrataḥ
english: Understanding Rāma's words, Sumitrā's son, the joy of his friends, took leave of Guha and the charioteer and stood before his brother.

sanskrit: tataḥ kalāpān saṃnahya khaḍgau baddhvā ca dhanvinau jagmatur yena tau gaṅgāṃ sītayā saha rāghavau
english: Then, fastening their quivers and girding on their swords, the two Rāghavas, bearing bows, went together with Sītā toward the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: rāmam eva tu dharmajñam upagamya vinītavat kim ahaṃ karavāṇīti sūtaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
english: The charioteer, approaching Rāma — that knower of dharma — humbly with palms joined, said: "What shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: nivartasvety uvācainam etāvad dhi kṛtaṃ mama yānaṃ vihāya padbhyāṃ tu gamiṣyāmo mahāvanam
english: "Turn back" — so he told him — "this much has been done for me. Leaving the chariot behind, we shall go on foot into the great forest."

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ tv abhyanujñātam avekṣyārtaḥ sa sārathiḥ sumantraḥ puruṣavyāghram aikṣvākam idam abravīt
english: Then the charioteer Sumantra, distressed to see himself thus dismissed, spoke these words to the tiger among men, the Aikṣvāka prince.

sanskrit: nātikrāntam idaṃ loke puruṣeṇeha kena cit tava sabhrātṛbhāryasya vāsaḥ prākṛtavad vane
english: "No one in this world has ever surpassed this — that you, together with your brother and wife, should dwell in the forest like a common man."

sanskrit: na manye brahmacarye 'sti svadhīte vā phalodayaḥ mārdavārjavayor vāpi tvāṃ ced vyasanam āgatam
english: "I do not think there is any fruit in celibacy, in sacred study, or in gentleness and uprightness, if such misfortune has come upon you."

sanskrit: saha rāghava vaidehyā bhrātrā caiva vane vasan tvaṃ gatiṃ prāpsyase vīra trīṃl lokāṃs tu jayann iva
english: "Dwelling in the forest with the Vaidehī and your brother, you shall attain a station, O hero, as if conquering the three worlds."

sanskrit: vayaṃ khalu hatā rāma ye tayāpy upavañcitāḥ kaikeyyā vaśam eṣyāmaḥ pāpāyā duḥkhabhāginaḥ
english: "We are truly ruined, O Rāma, we who have been deceived by her — we shall come under the sway of that sinful Kaikeyī, sharers in sorrow."

sanskrit: iti bruvann ātma samaṃ sumantraḥ sārathis tadā dṛṣṭvā dura gataṃ rāmaṃ duḥkhārto rurude ciram
english: Speaking thus, the charioteer Sumantra — so dear to himself as Rāma was — seeing Rāma gone far away, wept long in his grief.

sanskrit: tatas tu vigate bāṣpe sūtaṃ spṛṣṭodakaṃ śucim rāmas tu madhuraṃ vākyaṃ punaḥ punar uvāca tam
english: Then, when his tears had subsided, Rāma spoke sweet words again and again to the charioteer, who had touched water and was ritually pure.

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ tvayā tulyaṃ suhṛdaṃ nopalakṣaye yathā daśaratho rājā māṃ na śocet tathā kuru
english: "I see no friend equal to you among the Ikṣvākus. Do what must be done so that King Daśaratha does not grieve for me."

sanskrit: śokopahata cetāś ca vṛddhaś ca jagatīpatiḥ kāma bhārāvasannaś ca tasmād etad bravīmi te
english: "The lord of the earth is stricken in mind by grief, he is old, and he is weighed down by the burden of desire — it is for that reason I say this to you."

sanskrit: yad yad ājñāpayet kiṃ cit sa mahātmā mahīpatiḥ kaikeyyāḥ priyakāmārthaṃ kāryaṃ tad avikāṅkṣayā
english: "Whatever the great-souled lord of the earth may command, whatever must be done for the sake of gratifying Kaikeyī's wish, do that without hesitation."

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ hi rājyāni praśāsati nareśvarāḥ yad eṣāṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu mano na pratihanyate
english: "For this purpose do kings rule their kingdoms — that their minds are not thwarted in any of their undertakings."

sanskrit: tad yathā sa mahārājo nālīkam adhigacchati na ca tāmyati duḥkhena sumantra kuru tat tathā
english: "So do what must be done, Sumantra, that the great king does not suffer reproach, nor does he faint from sorrow."

sanskrit: adṛṣṭaduḥkhaṃ rājānaṃ vṛddham āryaṃ jitendriyam brūyās tvam abhivādyaiva mama hetor idaṃ vacaḥ
english: "Having saluted him, you should speak these words to the king on my behalf — to that king who has not known such sorrow before, who is old, noble, and master of his senses."

sanskrit: naivāham anuśocāmi lakṣmaṇo na ca maithilī ayodhyāyāś cyutāś ceti vane vatsyāmaheti vā
english: "Neither I grieve, nor Lakṣmaṇa, nor the Maithilī — neither at having been cast out from Ayodhyā, nor at dwelling in the forest."

sanskrit: caturdaśasu varṣeṣu nivṛtteṣu punaḥ punaḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ māṃ ca sītāṃ ca drakṣyasi kṣipram āgatān
english: "Once the fourteen years have passed, you will soon see Lakṣmaṇa, me, and Sītā returned again."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu rājānaṃ mātaraṃ ca sumantra me anyāś ca devīḥ sahitāḥ kaikeyīṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having thus addressed the king, greet my mother, and the other queens together, including Kaikeyī, again and again.

sanskrit: ārogyaṃ brūhi kausalyām atha pādābhivandanam sītāyā mama cāryasya vacanāl lakṣmaṇasya ca
english: "Convey wishes of good health to Kausalyā and the salutation at her feet — from Sītā, from me, and at the word of the noble Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: brūyāś ca hi mahārājaṃ bharataṃ kṣipram ānaya āgataś cāpi bharataḥ sthāpyo nṛpamate pade
english: "Tell the great king: 'Bring Bharata quickly.' And when Bharata has come, he must be established in the royal office according to the king's wish."

sanskrit: bharataṃ ca pariṣvajya yauvarājye 'bhiṣicya ca asmatsaṃtāpajaṃ duḥkhaṃ na tvām abhibhaviṣyati
english: "Having embraced Bharata and consecrated him as crown prince, the sorrow born of grief for us will no longer overpower you."

sanskrit: bharataś cāpi vaktavyo yathā rājani vartase tathā mātṛṣu vartethāḥ sarvāsv evāviśeṣataḥ
english: "Bharata too must be told: 'As you conduct yourself toward the king, so you must conduct yourself toward all the mothers without distinction.'"

sanskrit: yathā ca tava kaikeyī sumitrā cāviśeṣataḥ tathaiva devī kausalyā mama mātā viśeṣataḥ
english: "Just as Kaikeyī and Sumitrā are for you without distinction, so too must Queen Kausalyā be honored — she is my mother especially."

sanskrit: nivartyamāno rāmeṇa sumantraḥ śokakarśitaḥ tat sarvaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā snehāt kākutstham abravīt
english: Being dismissed by Rāma and emaciated by grief, Sumantra, having heard all those words, spoke out of affection to the Kākutstha.

sanskrit: yad ahaṃ nopacāreṇa brūyāṃ snehād aviklavaḥ bhaktimān iti tat tāvad vākyaṃ tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi
english: "Whatever I might say out of devotion and unguarded love — without ceremony, without distress — you must forgive those words of a loyal servant."

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi tvadvihīno 'haṃ pratiyāsyāmi tāṃ purīm tava tāta viyogena putraśokākulām iva
english: "How shall I, bereft of you, return to that city which, dear one, is like one overwhelmed by the grief of losing a son, on account of your separation?"

sanskrit: sarāmam api tāvan me rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā janaḥ vinā rāmaṃ rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidīryetāpi sā purī
english: "When the people saw the chariot with Rāma on it, how will the city bear seeing the chariot now without Rāma — it would shatter at the sight."

sanskrit: dainyaṃ hi nagarī gacched dṛṣṭvā śūnyam imaṃ ratham sūtāvaśeṣaṃ svaṃ sainyaṃ hatavīram ivāhave
english: "The city will sink into anguish seeing this empty chariot with only the charioteer remaining — like an army that has lost its hero in battle."

sanskrit: dūre 'pi nivasantaṃ tvāṃ mānasenāgrataḥ sthitam cintayantyo 'dya nūnaṃ tvāṃ nirāhārāḥ kṛtāḥ prajāḥ
english: "The people, thinking of you dwelling afar yet standing before them in their minds, have surely gone without food today."

sanskrit: ārtanādo hi yaḥ paurair muktas tadvipravāsane rathasthaṃ māṃ niśāmyaiva kuryuḥ śataguṇaṃ tataḥ
english: "The cry of anguish that the citizens raised at the time of your exile — on seeing me seated in the chariot, they will raise it a hundredfold."

sanskrit: ahaṃ kiṃ cāpi vakṣyāmi devīṃ tava suto mayā nīto 'sau mātulakulaṃ saṃtāpaṃ mā kṛthā iti
english: "And what shall I say to the queen — 'Your son has been taken by me to his maternal uncle's house; do not grieve'? How could I say even this?"

sanskrit: asatyam api naivāhaṃ brūyāṃ vacanam īdṛśam katham apriyam evāhaṃ brūyāṃ satyam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: "I would not speak even a falsehood of that kind. And how shall I speak this truth, which is so painful?"

sanskrit: mama tāvan niyogasthās tvadbandhujanavāhinaḥ kathaṃ rathaṃ tvayā hīnaṃ pravakṣyanti hayottamāḥ
english: "These excellent horses that serve at my command, that have carried your kinsmen — how will they draw the chariot bereft of you?"

sanskrit: yadi me yācamānasya tyāgam eva kariṣyasi saratho 'gniṃ pravekṣyāmi tyakta mātra iha tvayā
english: "If you resolve to abandon even me though I beg you, then the moment you forsake me here, I shall enter fire together with the chariot."

sanskrit: bhaviṣyanti vane yāni tapovighnakarāṇi te rathena pratibādhiṣye tāni sattvāni rāghava
english: "Whatever creatures in the forest might disturb your austerities, I will ward them off with the chariot, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: tat kṛtena mayā prāptaṃ ratha caryā kṛtaṃ sukham āśaṃse tvatkṛtenāhaṃ vanavāsakṛtaṃ sukham
english: "The comfort I have gained from the service of the chariot — I aspire now to the comfort of forest-dwelling, done for your sake."

sanskrit: prasīdecchāmi te 'raṇye bhavituṃ pratyanantaraḥ prītyābhihitam icchāmi bhava me patyanantaraḥ
english: "Be pleased to let me be next to you in the forest. I wish to be told with affection: 'Be next to my lord.'"

sanskrit: tava śuśrūṣaṇaṃ mūrdhnā kariṣyāmi vane vasan ayodhyāṃ devalokaṃ vā sarvathā prajahāmy aham
english: "I will with bowed head render service to you, dwelling in the forest. Ayodhyā and the world of the gods — I abandon them both entirely."

sanskrit: na hi śakyā praveṣṭuṃ sā mayāyodhyā tvayā vinā rājadhānī mahendrasya yathā duṣkṛtakarmaṇā
english: "I cannot enter that Ayodhyā without you — just as an evildoer cannot enter the capital of great Indra."

sanskrit: ime cāpi hayā vīra yadi te vanavāsinaḥ paricaryāṃ kariṣyanti prāpsyanti paramāṃ gatim
english: "These horses too, O hero — if they serve you while you dwell in the forest, they will attain the highest state."

sanskrit: vanavāse kṣayaṃ prāpte mamaiṣa hi manorathaḥ yad anena rathenaiva tvāṃ vaheyaṃ purīṃ punaḥ
english: "When the period of forest-dwelling has come to an end, this is my heart's desire: to carry you back to the city in this very chariot."

sanskrit: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi sahitasya tvayā vane kṣaṇabhūtāni yāsyanti śataśas tu tato 'nyathā
english: "The fourteen years spent in the forest in your company will pass like a moment; whereas otherwise they would stretch like hundreds of years."

sanskrit: bhṛtyavatsala tiṣṭhantaṃ bhartṛputragate pathi bhaktaṃ bhṛtyaṃ sthitaṃ sthityāṃ tvaṃ na māṃ hātum arhasi
english: "O lord who loves your servants — one who is devoted, who stands steadfast in his duty, who stands in the path that follows the master's son — you should not abandon me."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dīnaṃ yācamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ rāmo bhṛtyānukampī tu sumantram idam abravīt
english: When Sumantra begged thus piteously in many ways again and again, Rāma, who was compassionate toward his servants, spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: jānāmi paramāṃ bhaktiṃ mayi te bhartṛvatsala śṛṇu cāpi yadarthaṃ tvāṃ preṣayāmi purīm itaḥ
english: "I know your supreme devotion toward me, O one devoted to your master. Listen also to the reason why I am sending you back to the city from here."

sanskrit: nagarīṃ tvāṃ gataṃ dṛṣṭvā jananī me yavīyasī kaikeyī pratyayaṃ gacched iti rāmo vanaṃ gataḥ
english: "When she sees you returned to the city, my younger mother Kaikeyī will gain confidence that Rāma has indeed gone to the forest."

sanskrit: parituṣṭā hi sā devi vanavāsaṃ gate mayi rājānaṃ nātiśaṅketa mithyāvādīti dhārmikam
english: "For when I have gone to dwell in the forest, that queen, being satisfied, would not unduly suspect the righteous king of speaking falsely."

sanskrit: eṣa me prathamaḥ kalpo yad ambā me yavīyasī bharatārakṣitaṃ sphītaṃ putrarājyam avāpnuyāt
english: "This is my foremost consideration: that my younger mother should obtain the prosperous kingdom safe under the rule of her son Bharata."

sanskrit: mama priyārthaṃ rājñaś ca sarathas tvaṃ purīṃ vraja saṃdiṣṭaś cāsi yān arthāṃs tāṃs tān brūyās tathātathā
english: "For my sake and for the king's sake, go to the city with the chariot. And convey the various messages you have been charged with, just as I have told you."

sanskrit: ity uktvā vacanaṃ sūtaṃ sāntvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ guhaṃ vacanam aklībaṃ rāmo hetumad abravīt jaṭāḥ kṛtvā gamiṣyāmi nyagrodhakṣīram ānaya
english: Having spoken thus and comforted the charioteer again and again, Rāma spoke firm and reasoned words to Guha: "I shall make matted locks and go — bring me the sap of the nyagrodha tree."

sanskrit: tat kṣīraṃ rājaputrāya guhaḥ kṣipram upāharat lakṣmaṇasyātmanaś caiva rāmas tenākaroj jaṭāḥ
english: Guha quickly brought that sap to the prince. With it, Rāma made matted locks for Lakṣmaṇa and for himself.

sanskrit: tau tadā cīravasanau jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇau aśobhetām ṛṣisamau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Then the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, clad in bark garments and bearing coils of matted hair, shone like sages.

sanskrit: tato vaikhānasaṃ mārgam āsthitaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ vratam ādiṣṭavān rāmaḥ sahāyaṃ guham abravīt
english: Then, having entered the path of the forest-ascetics together with Lakṣmaṇa and enjoined his vow, Rāma spoke to his companion Guha.

sanskrit: apramatto bale kośe durge janapade tathā bhavethā guha rājyaṃ hi durārakṣatamaṃ matam
english: "Be ever vigilant, Guha, in matters of army, treasury, the fort, and the countryside — for a kingdom is held to be the most difficult thing to guard."

sanskrit: tatas taṃ samanujñāya guham ikṣvākunandanaḥ jagāma tūrṇam avyagraḥ sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Then, having taken leave of Guha, the delight of the Ikṣvākus departed swiftly and undistracted, with his wife and together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvā nadītīre nāvam ikṣvākunandanaḥ titīrṣuḥ śīghragāṃ gaṅgām idaṃ lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Seeing a boat on the bank of the river, the delight of the Ikṣvākus, wishing to cross the swift-flowing Gaṅgā, spoke thus to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: āroha tvaṃ nara vyāghra sthitāṃ nāvam imāṃ śanaiḥ sītāṃ cāropayānvakṣaṃ parigṛhya manasvinīm
english: "Board this waiting boat gently, O tiger among men, and help the noble-minded Sītā on board, holding her close to you."

sanskrit: sa bhrātuḥ śāsanaṃ śrutvā sarvam apratikūlayan āropya maithilīṃ pūrvam ārurohātmavāṃs tataḥ
english: Hearing his brother's instruction and not opposing any of it, he first helped the Maithilī on board, and then the self-controlled one climbed up himself.

sanskrit: athāruroha tejasvī svayaṃ lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ tato niṣādādhipatir guho jñātīn acodayat
english: Then the radiant one, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, himself boarded; after that the lord of the Niṣādas, Guha, urged his kinsmen on.

sanskrit: anujñāya sumantraṃ ca sabalaṃ caiva taṃ guham āsthāya nāvaṃ rāmas tu codayām āsa nāvikān
english: Having bidden farewell to Sumantra and to Guha along with his forces, Rāma boarded the boat and urged on the boatmen.

sanskrit: tatas taiś coditā sā nauḥ karṇadhārasamāhitā śubhasphyavegābhihatā śīghraṃ salilam atyagāt
english: Then, urged by them, the boat, steered by the helmsman and driven by the swift strokes of well-crafted oars, quickly crossed the waters.

sanskrit: madhyaṃ tu samanuprāpya bhāgīrathyās tv aninditā vaidehī prāñjalir bhūtvā tāṃ nadīm idam abravīt
english: Reaching the middle of the Bhāgīrathī, the blameless Vaidehī, joining her palms in reverence, spoke these words to that river.

sanskrit: putro daśarathasyāyaṃ mahārājasya dhīmataḥ nideśaṃ pālayatv enaṃ gaṅge tvadabhirakṣitaḥ
english: "This son of the wise great king Daśaratha — may he fulfill the command, O Gaṅgā, protected by you."

sanskrit: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi samagrāṇy uṣya kānane bhrātrā saha mayā caiva punaḥ pratyāgamiṣyati
english: "Having dwelt in the forest for a full fourteen years with his brother and with me, he will return again."

sanskrit: tatas tvāṃ devi subhage kṣemeṇa punar āgatā yakṣye pramuditā gaṅge sarvakāmasamṛddhaye
english: "Then, O auspicious goddess, having returned safely, I shall joyfully worship you, O Gaṅgā, for the fulfillment of all desires."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi tripathagā devi brahma lokaṃ samīkṣase bhāryā codadhirājasya loke 'smin saṃpradṛśyase
english: "For you, O goddess, flow in three worlds and behold the realm of Brahmā; you are known in this world as the wife of the lord of the ocean."

sanskrit: sā tvāṃ devi namasyāmi praśaṃsāmi ca śobhane prāpta rājye naravyāghra śivena punar āgate
english: "I salute you, O goddess, and praise you, O beautiful one, when the tiger among men has returned safely after regaining his kingdom."

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi vastrāṇy annaṃ ca peśalam brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradāsyāmi tava priyacikīrṣayā
english: "Hundreds of thousands of cows, fine garments, and food — I shall give these to Brāhmaṇas out of my desire to please you."

sanskrit: tathā saṃbhāṣamāṇā sā sītā gaṅgām aninditā dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇaṃ tīraṃ kṣipram evābhyupāgamat
english: Speaking thus, the blameless Sītā, turning to the right, quickly reached the right bank.

sanskrit: tīraṃ tu samanuprāpya nāvaṃ hitvā nararṣabhaḥ prātiṣṭhata saha bhrātrā vaidehyā ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having reached the far bank and leaving the boat behind, the bull among men, the scorcher of foes, set forth together with his brother and the Vaidehī.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahābāhuḥ sumitrānandavardhanam agrato gaccha saumitre sītā tvām anugacchatu
english: Then the mighty-armed one spoke to the joy-increaser of Sumitrā: "Go ahead, O Saumitri; let Sītā follow you."

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato 'haṃ gamiṣyāmi tvāṃ ca sītāṃ ca pālayan adya duḥkhaṃ tu vaidehī vanavāsasya vetsyati
english: "I shall go behind, guarding both you and Sītā. Today the Vaidehī will come to know the hardship of forest life."

sanskrit: gataṃ tu gaṅgāparapāram āśu rāmaṃ sumantraḥ pratataṃ nirīkṣya adhvaprakarṣād vinivṛttadṛṣṭir mumoca bāṣpaṃ vyathitas tapasvī
english: But Sumantra, that wretched one, gazing steadily at Rāma who had quickly crossed to the far bank of the Gaṅgā, with his gaze finally turned back by the distance of the road, shed tears in his anguish.

sanskrit: tau tatra hatvā caturo mahāmṛgān varāham ṛśyaṃ pṛṣataṃ mahārurum ādāya medhyaṃ tvaritaṃ bubhukṣitau vāsāya kāle yayatur vanaspatim
english: Those two, having slain four great forest animals there — a boar, a ṛśya antelope, a spotted deer, and a large deer — took the pure meat and, being hungry, quickly went at the proper time to a tree for shelter.

sanskrit: sa taṃ vṛkṣaṃ samāsādya saṃdhyām anvāsya paścimām rāmo ramayatāṃ śreṣṭha iti hovāca lakṣmaṇam
english: Having reached that tree and performed the evening twilight rite, Rāma, best among those who bring delight, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: adyeyaṃ prathamā rātrir yātā janapadād bahiḥ yā sumantreṇa rahitā tāṃ notkaṇṭhitum arhasi
english: "This is the first night spent outside the inhabited land, away from Sumantra — you should not be anxious about it."

sanskrit: jāgartavyam atandribhyām adya prabhṛti rātriṣu yogakṣemo hi sītāyā vartate lakṣmaṇāvayoḥ
english: "From this day forward we must both keep vigil through the nights without slackness, for the safety and well-being of Sītā rests on us."

sanskrit: rātriṃ kathaṃ cid evemāṃ saumitre vartayāmahe upāvartāmahe bhūmāv āstīrya svayam ārjitaiḥ
english: "Somehow, Saumitri, we shall pass this night, lying down on the ground on what we have gathered ourselves."

sanskrit: sa tu saṃviśya medinyāṃ mahārhaśayanocitaḥ imāḥ saumitraye rāmo vyājahāra kathāḥ śubhāḥ
english: Lying down on the earth — he who was accustomed to beds of the highest worth — Rāma spoke these auspicious words to Saumitri.

sanskrit: dhruvam adya mahārājo duḥkhaṃ svapiti lakṣmaṇa kṛtakāmā tu kaikeyī tuṣṭā bhavitum arhati
english: "Surely the great king sleeps in sorrow tonight, Lakṣmaṇa. But Kaikeyī, having achieved her desire, is fit to be satisfied."

sanskrit: sā hi devī mahārājaṃ kaikeyī rājyakāraṇāt api na cyāvayet prāṇān dṛṣṭvā bharatam āgatam
english: "For that queen Kaikeyī, for the sake of the kingdom, would not even spare the life of the great king — not even when she sees Bharata arrived."

sanskrit: anāthaś caiva vṛddhaś ca mayā caiva vinākṛtaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati kāmātmā kaikeyyā vaśam āgataḥ
english: "Helpless, old, bereft of me, and enslaved to desire, come under Kaikeyī's control — what will the king do?"

sanskrit: idaṃ vyasanam ālokya rājñaś ca mativibhramam kāma evārdhadharmābhyāṃ garīyān iti me matiḥ
english: "Looking at this calamity and at the king's confusion of mind, I think desire is greater than both wealth and dharma."

sanskrit: ko hy avidvān api pumān pramadāyāḥ kṛte tyajet chandānuvartinaṃ putraṃ tāto mām iva lakṣmaṇa
english: "For what man, even an ignorant one, would for the sake of a woman abandon a son who follows his wishes — as our father has abandoned me, Lakṣmaṇa?"

sanskrit: sukhī bata sabhāryaś ca bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ muditān kosalān eko yo bhokṣyaty adhirājavat
english: "How fortunate Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, must be — with his wife beside him, he alone will enjoy the joyful Kosalas like an overlord."

sanskrit: sa hi sarvasya rājyasya mukham ekaṃ bhaviṣyati tāte ca vayasātīte mayi cāraṇyam āśrite
english: "For he will be the sole master of the whole kingdom, when our father has passed beyond his years and I have taken refuge in the forest."

sanskrit: arthadharmau parityajya yaḥ kāmam anuvartate evam āpadyate kṣipraṃ rājā daśaratho yathā
english: "One who abandons wealth and dharma and follows desire alone quickly meets such ruin as King Daśaratha has met."

sanskrit: manye daśarathāntāya mama pravrājanāya ca kaikeyī saumya saṃprāptā rājyāya bharatasya ca
english: "I believe that Kaikeyī has come to bring about the end of Daśaratha, my banishment, and the kingdom for Bharata, O gentle one."

sanskrit: apīdānīṃ na kaikeyī saubhāgyamadamohitā kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca saṃprabādheta matkṛte
english: "I only hope that Kaikeyī, intoxicated by the pride of her good fortune, does not now oppress Kausalyā and Sumitrā on my account."

sanskrit: mā sma matkāraṇād devī sumitrā duḥkham āvaset ayodhyām ita eva tvaṃ kāle praviśa lakṣmaṇa
english: "Let not Queen Sumitrā suffer grief on my account. You should enter Ayodhyā from here when the time comes, Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: aham eko gamiṣyāmi sītayā saha daṇḍakān anāthāyā hi nāthas tvaṃ kausalyāyā bhaviṣyasi
english: "I alone will go to the Daṇḍakas with Sītā. For you will be the protector of Kausalyā, who would otherwise be without protector."

sanskrit: kṣudrakarmā hi kaikeyī dveṣād anyāyyam ācaret paridadyā hi dharmajñe bharate mama mātaram
english: "For Kaikeyī, given to petty acts, might out of hatred do what is unjust. You must entrust my mother to the dharma-knowing Bharata."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ jātyantare kasmiṃ striyaḥ putrair viyojitāḥ jananyā mama saumitre tad apy etad upasthitam
english: "Surely in some past life women were separated from their sons — and now that same fate has come upon my mother, Saumitri."

sanskrit: mayā hi cirapuṣṭena duḥkhasaṃvardhitena ca viprāyujyata kausalyā phalakāle dhig astu mām
english: "Kausalyā, who nurtured me for so long and raised me through suffering, is now separated from me at the time of bearing fruit — shame on me!"

sanskrit: mā sma sīmantinī kā cij janayet putram īdṛśam saumitre yo 'ham ambāyā dadmi śokam anantakam
english: "Let no woman, Saumitri, ever give birth to a son like me, who brings endless grief to his mother."

sanskrit: manye prītiviśiṣṭā sā matto lakṣmaṇasārikā yasyās tac chrūyate vākyaṃ śuka pādam arer daśa
english: "I think that myna bird of Lakṣmaṇa is more blessed than I am — the one from whom those words are heard: 'Parrot, bite the foot of the enemy.'"

sanskrit: śocantyāś cālpabhāgyāyā na kiṃ cid upakurvatā purtreṇa kim aputrāyā mayā kāryam ariṃdama
english: "What use is a son to one who is without son's benefit — to my grieving, ill-fortuned mother, when I have done nothing to help her, O subduer of foes?"

sanskrit: alpabhāgyā hi me mātā kausalyā rahitā mayā śete paramaduḥkhārtā patitā śokasāgare
english: "Ill-fated is my mother Kausalyā, bereft of me — she lies stricken with the deepest sorrow, fallen into an ocean of grief."

sanskrit: eko hy aham ayodhyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇa tareyam iṣubhiḥ kruddho nanu vīryam akāraṇam
english: "I alone, were I angry, could overcome Ayodhyā and the whole earth with my arrows — though valor without cause is no virtue, Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: adharmabhaya bhītaś ca paralokasya cānagha tena lakṣmaṇa nādyāham ātmānam abhiṣecaye
english: "But I am afraid of unrighteousness and afraid for the other world, O sinless one — it is for that reason, Lakṣmaṇa, that I do not consecrate myself today."

sanskrit: etad anyac ca karuṇaṃ vilapya vijane bahu aśrupūrṇamukho rāmaḥ niśi tūṣṇīm upāviśat
english: Lamenting thus and in many other piteous ways in that lonely place, his face full of tears, Rāma sat down in silence in the night.

sanskrit: vilapyoparataṃ rāmaṃ gatārciṣam ivānalam samudram iva nirvegam āśvāsayata lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa comforted Rāma when he had finished his lament — like a fire whose flames have died down, like an ocean whose waves have stilled.

sanskrit: dhruvam adya purī rāma ayodhyā yudhināṃ vara niṣprabhā tvayi niṣkrānte gatacandreva śarvarī
english: "Surely today, O Rāma, O best among warriors, the city of Ayodhyā is without luster since your departure — like a night bereft of the moon."

sanskrit: naitad aupayikaṃ rāma yad idaṃ paritapyase viṣādayasi sītāṃ ca māṃ caiva puruṣarṣabha
english: "It is not fitting, O Rāma, that you should torment yourself thus and grieve both Sītā and me, O bull among men."

sanskrit: na ca sītā tvayā hīnā na cāham api rāghava muhūrtam api jīvāvo jalān matsyāv ivoddhṛtau
english: "Neither Sītā without you nor I without you, O Rāghava, could live even for a moment — like fish drawn out of water."

sanskrit: na hi tātaṃ na śatrughnaṃ na sumitrāṃ paraṃtapa draṣṭum iccheyam adyāhaṃ svargaṃ vāpi tvayā vinā
english: "I would not wish to see our father, nor Śatrughna, nor Sumitrā, O scorcher of foes, nor even heaven itself without you."

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇasyottama puṣkalaṃ vaco niśamya caivaṃ vanavāsam ādarāt samāḥ samastā vidadhe paraṃtapaḥ prapadya dharmaṃ sucirāya rāghavaḥ
english: Hearing these noble and full words of Lakṣmaṇa, the Rāghava, that scorcher of foes, having embraced dharma for a long time, composed himself with reverence for all the years of forest life ahead.

sanskrit: te tu tasmin mahāvṛkṣa uṣitvā rajanīṃ śivām vimale 'bhyudite sūrye tasmād deśāt pratasthire
english: Having spent the auspicious night at that great tree, when the pure sun had risen, they departed from that place.

sanskrit: yatra bhāgīrathī gaṅgā yamunām abhivartate jagmus taṃ deśam uddiśya vigāhya sumahad vanam
english: They went toward the place where the Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā approaches the Yamunā, penetrating deep into the great forest.

sanskrit: te bhūmim āgān vividhān deśāṃś cāpi manoramān adṛṣṭapūrvān paśyantas tatra tatra yaśasvinaḥ
english: Those illustrious ones came upon the earth through various regions — charming places never seen before — beholding them here and there.

sanskrit: yathākṣemeṇa gacchan sa paśyaṃś ca vividhān drumān nivṛttamātre divase rāmaḥ saumitrim abravīt
english: Proceeding at ease and observing various trees, when the day had just turned, Rāma spoke to Saumitri.

sanskrit: prayāgam abhitaḥ paśya saumitre dhūmam unnatam agner bhagavataḥ ketuṃ manye saṃnihito muniḥ
english: "Look around Prayāga, Saumitri, at the tall column of smoke — the banner of the sacred fire. I think the sage is nearby."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ prāptāḥ sma saṃbhedaṃ gaṅgāyamunayor vayam tathā hi śrūyate śambdo vāriṇā vārighaṭṭitaḥ
english: "Surely we have reached the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā — for the sound of water meeting water is heard."

sanskrit: dārūṇi paribhinnāni vanajair upajīvibhiḥ bharadvājāśrame caite dṛśyante vividhā drumāḥ
english: "Wood cut by those who live off the forest, and these various trees are visible — this is the hermitage of Bharadvāja."

sanskrit: dhanvinau tau sukhaṃ gatvā lambamāne divākare gaṅgāyamunayoḥ saṃdhau prāpatur nilayaṃ muneḥ
english: Those two bearing bows, traveling comfortably as the sun hung low, reached the abode of the sage at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

sanskrit: rāmas tv āśramam āsādya trāsayan mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ gatvā muhūrtam adhvānaṃ bharadvājam upāgamat
english: Rāma, having approached the hermitage and startling the deer and birds, walked a moment's distance and came to Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tatas tv āśramam āsādya muner darśanakāṅkṣiṇau sītayānugatau vīrau dūrād evāvatasthatuḥ
english: Then the two heroes, wishing to see the sage, having approached the hermitage with Sītā following them, stood at a respectful distance.

sanskrit: hutāgnihotraṃ dṛṣṭvaiva mahābhāgaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sītayā cābhyavādayat
english: Seeing the great one who had offered his agnihotra oblation, Rāma, with joined palms, together with Saumitri and with Sītā, saluted him.

sanskrit: nyavedayata cātmānaṃ tasmai lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ putrau daśarathasyāvāṃ bhagavan rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: The elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa presented himself to him: "We two are the sons of Daśaratha, O venerable one — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: bhāryā mameyaṃ vaidehī kalyāṇī janakātmajā māṃ cānuyātā vijanaṃ tapovanam aninditā
english: "This is my wife, the Vaidehī, the auspicious daughter of Janaka — blameless, she has followed me into this desolate forest hermitage."

sanskrit: pitrā pravrājyamānaṃ māṃ saumitrir anujaḥ priyaḥ ayam anvagamad bhrātā vanam eva dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: "As I was being sent into exile by my father, this dear younger brother Saumitri, firm in his vow, followed me into the very forest."

sanskrit: pitrā niyuktā bhagavan praveṣyāmas tapovanam dharmam evācariṣyāmas tatra mūlaphalāśanāḥ
english: "Commanded by our father, O venerable one, we shall enter the forest hermitage; there we shall practice dharma alone, subsisting on roots and fruits."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ upānayata dharmātmā gām arghyam udakaṃ tataḥ
english: Hearing those words of the wise prince, the righteous-souled one then brought forth a cow, arghya water, and drinking water.

sanskrit: mṛgapakṣibhir āsīno munibhiś ca samantataḥ rāmam āgatam abhyarcya svāgatenāha taṃ muniḥ
english: Surrounded on all sides by deer, birds, and sages, the sage honored Rāma on his arrival and welcomed him with the word of welcome.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tām arcām upaviṣṭaṃ sarāghavam bharadvājo 'bravīd vākyaṃ dharmayuktam idaṃ tadā
english: Having received that honor, Bharadvāja then spoke these dharma-filled words to Rāma as he sat down together with his companions.

sanskrit: cirasya khalu kākutstha paśyāmi tvām ihāgatam śrutaṃ tava mayā cedaṃ vivāsanam akāraṇam
english: "At long last, O Kākutstha, I see you arrived here. I have heard of this causeless exile of yours."

sanskrit: avakāśo vivikto 'yaṃ mahānadyoḥ samāgame puṇyaś ca ramaṇīyaś ca vasatv iha bhagān sukham
english: "This spot is secluded, at the confluence of two great rivers — sacred and beautiful. May your honor dwell here in happiness."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vacanaṃ bharadvājena rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ rāmaḥ sarvahite rataḥ
english: Being thus spoken to by Bharadvāja, the Rāghava Rāma, devoted to the welfare of all, replied with auspicious words.

sanskrit: bhagavann ita āsannaḥ paurajānapado janaḥ āgamiṣyati vaidehīṃ māṃ cāpi prekṣako janaḥ anena kāraṇenāham iha vāsaṃ na rocaye
english: "O venerable one, the people of the city and countryside are close by here; crowds will come to gaze upon the Vaidehī and upon me. For this reason I am not pleased to dwell here."

sanskrit: ekānte paśya bhagavann āśramasthānam uttamam ramate yatra vaidehī sukhārhā janakātmajā
english: "Look, O venerable one, for an excellent and solitary hermitage-place where the Vaidehī, the daughter of Janaka who deserves happiness, may find delight."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ rāghavasya tato vākyam artha grāhakam abravīt
english: Hearing these auspicious words of the Rāghava, the great sage Bharadvāja then spoke words that grasped his meaning.

sanskrit: daśakrośa itas tāta girir yasmin nivatsyasi maharṣisevitaḥ puṇyaḥ sarvataḥ sukha darśanaḥ
english: "Ten krośas from here, dear one, is a mountain where you shall dwell — sacred, frequented by great sages, pleasant to behold from every side."

sanskrit: golāṅgūlānucarito vānararkṣaniṣevitaḥ citrakūṭa iti khyāto gandhamādanasaṃnibhaḥ
english: "Roamed by golāṅgūla monkeys, frequented by monkeys and bears — known as Citrakūṭa, it resembles the Gandhamādana mountain."

sanskrit: yāvatā citra kūṭasya naraḥ śṛṅgāṇy avekṣate kalyāṇāni samādhatte na pāpe kurute manaḥ
english: "As long as a person looks upon the peaks of Citrakūṭa, his mind settles in what is auspicious and does not turn toward evil."

sanskrit: ṛṣayas tatra bahavo vihṛtya śaradāṃ śatam tapasā divam ārūḍhāḥ kapālaśirasā saha
english: "Many sages there, having sported through hundreds of autumns, have ascended to heaven through austerity — together with Kapālaśiras."

sanskrit: praviviktam ahaṃ manye taṃ vāsaṃ bhavataḥ sukham iha vā vanavāsāya vasa rāma mayā saha
english: "I think that secluded dwelling will be pleasant for you — or else dwell here for your forest sojourn with me, O Rāma."

sanskrit: sa rāmaṃ sarvakāmais taṃ bharadvājaḥ priyātithim sabhāryaṃ saha ca bhrātrā pratijagrāha dharmavit
english: That knower of dharma, Bharadvāja, received Rāma — that beloved guest — together with his wife and brother, with all manner of hospitalities.

sanskrit: tasya prayāge rāmasya taṃ maharṣim upeyuṣaḥ prapannā rajanī puṇyā citrāḥ kathayataḥ kathāḥ
english: For Rāma, having come to Prayāga and arrived at that great sage, the sacred night passed by as they told various tales.

sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu bharadvājam upāgamat uvāca naraśārdūlo muniṃ jvalitatejasaṃ
english: When the night had brightened into dawn, the tiger among men came to Bharadvāja and spoke to the sage of blazing splendor.

sanskrit: śarvarīṃ bhavanann adya satyaśīla tavāśrame uṣitāḥ smeha vasatim anujānātu no bhavān
english: "O one of truthful nature, this night just dawning — we have spent it here in your hermitage. May your honor grant us leave for our dwelling."

sanskrit: rātryāṃ tu tasyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ bharadvājo 'bravīd idam madhumūlaphalopetaṃ citrakūṭaṃ vrajeti ha
english: When that night had been passed, Bharadvāja spoke thus: "Go to Citrakūṭa, which abounds in honey, roots, and fruits."

sanskrit: tatra kuñjarayūthāni mṛgayūthāni cābhitaḥ vicaranti vanānteṣu tāni drakṣyasi rāghava
english: "There herds of elephants and herds of deer roam on every side through the forest glades — you will see them, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭakoyaṣṭikakokilasvanair vināditaṃ taṃ vasudhādharaṃ śivam mṛgaiś ca mattair bahubhiś ca kuñjaraiḥ suramyam āsādya samāvasāśramam
english: "Reaching that auspicious mountain, resounding with the cries of delighted koyaṣṭika birds and kokila cuckoos, filled with intoxicated deer and many elephants — most beautiful — set up your hermitage and dwell there."
